messages:
maria: heads up — support got an enterprise escalation: customer reports p95/p99 spike on text-gen API starting ~09:10 UTC. Saw retries and 504s. They attached traces and a couple of req ids. :frowning:

ajay: pinging infra, any cluster-side alerts?

infra-bot: alert: gpu-memory-pressure-high on pool-prod-eu-3 (90%+ for 3m) — triggered at 09:08 UTC

kai: I pulled the request traces. p50 OK, p95 ~2.4s -> 5.6s, p99 up to 12s for a subset of requests that have long context and large batch_token_count. Looks correlated to nodes with recent OOMs.

lucy: customer-repro: they send intermittent long-context chats (up to 20k tokens), and also occasional heavy embedding jobs against same model. Could be KV growth?

ajay: gpu OOMs cause fallback to CPU for the process or aborted request? Our runtime tries to allocate, if CUDA fails we catch and retry on same node a couple times -> that causes retries + queuing.

maria: attached logs from their request ids:```
2028-03-12T09:10:21Z ERROR allocation.cu:213 cudamalloc failed: out of memory
2028-03-12T09:10:21Z WARN request-manager: retrying request (1/2) after allocation failure
2028-03-12T09:10:22Z INFO runtime-batcher: queued for retry on node i-0abc123 (gpu0)
2028-03-12T09:10:33Z ERROR request-timeout: request exceeded 10s
```

kai: also seeing big fragmentation metrics on affected GPUs. nvml snapshots show high external fragmentation and peak reserved > allocated.

ajay: quick question — did we recently change allocator flags or kernel build?

lucy: yes — we shipped allocator-tuning v2 last week which enabled aggressive async free + deferred coalesce. We also changed KV cache to retain by-user instead of by-session (to improve hit rate). Two correlated changes.

sre-oncall: timeline makes sense. KV retention increase -> more persistent KV pages -> higher resident memory. New allocator attempted to optimize but under sustained mixed workloads it fragments more.

maria: customer impact: intermittent p95/regressions and a couple 504s, revenue alert. They asked for mitigation asap.

ajay: proposed short-term mitigations (can ship within minutes):
- throttle long-context requests for this customer (max_context_tokens=8k)
- cap per-request KV retention (kv_pages_cap=256)
- reduce max_batch_tokens on the affected pool from 2048 -> 1024 to reduce peak allocs

kai: I can roll a canary that sets kv_pages_cap for pool-prod-eu-3 only. Also we can flip allocator flag to do eager free (rollback toggle).

lucy: canary sounds good. We should also avoid full node restarts unless necessary. Restart causes cold KV rebuilds which spike load.

ajay: repro steps for lab to reproduce:
1) run the long-context generator against model:redwood/llama-4-large with ctx=16k, concurrency=8, batch tokens ~1500
2) concurrently run embedding workload (dense) to create mixed alloc pattern
3) watch allocator metrics: alloc_failures, fragmentation_pct, kv_pages_total

commands:```
# run gen client
python perf_client.py --model llama-4-large --context 16000 --concurrency 8 --batch-tokens 1500 --run-id esk
# monitor nvml
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,name --format=csv -l 1
# runtime metrics
curl http://metrics:9090/api/v1/query?query=runtime_allocator_fragmentation_pct
```

kai: I ran that in the staging pool earlier and reproduced the retry pattern. Stack shows allocation failing in cudaMallocAsync and then allocator falls back to cudaMalloc which is slower and more fragment-prone.

maria: what are the risks of flipping allocator to eager free?

ajay: eager free reduces fragmentation but can increase peak memory churn and worsen tail latency for some short-lived bursts. But on these nodes where persistence is the issue, eager free + kv_pages_cap should help immediately. We can limit the flip to the single pool.

lucy: medium-term fixes: smarter KV eviction (LRU by request recency), size-aware batching, and a small allocator patch to pre-reserve large contiguous regions for long-context work (reduce fragmentation). Also consider per-tenant KV namespaces pinned to separate GPU sets.

sre-oncall: immediate action items:
- [ajay] deploy kv_pages_cap=256 to pool-prod-eu-3 as a canary (10 nodes) — ETA 10m
- [kai] flip allocator flag (defer_coalesce=false) on the same canary group — ETA 10m
- [lucy] throttle this customer's max_context to 8k via rate-limiter rule — ETA 5m
- [maria] notify customer about mitigation steps and expected reduced tail latency within ~10m

maria: I'll message support and update the ticket. cc @support-bot to mark as escalated.

deploy-bot: rolling config update to pool-prod-eu-3 (10 nodes): set runtime.kv_pages_cap=256 — started

infra-bot: deployment: config rollout succeeded on 10/10 nodes (pool-prod-eu-3-canary)

kai: flipped allocator flag on canary nodes and restarted runtime gracefully (no full GPU driver restart). Monitoring...

(2m later)

kai: early signs: p95 down from 5.6s -> 2.1s on canary nodes, p99 reduced from 12s -> 4.8s. Alloc failures dropped to near-zero.

maria: customer reported improvement: their p95 looks back to baseline on the routed traffic. They are happy for now. :relieved:

ajay: next steps (follow-up):
- run a full cluster rollout plan with automated health gates
- implement KV eviction policy change (LRU + size cap)
- bake allocator patch with contiguous reservation strategy and test in perf lab
- add per-request kv_pages metrics and per-tenant memory accounting
- create runbook entry for gpu-memory-pressure incidents and include these mitigations and repro steps

lucy: I'll create GH issues for KV eviction and allocator patch and link to this thread + perf artifacts.

maria: thanks team. saving logs/traces to the incident ticket. If anyone has other quick wins let me know. :thumbsup:
